scope: Connected original dormant Futex/Sleep admission: wake/requeue, deadline, signal, freezer, task/mm custody contention, cancellation and first byte/hardware View preparation.

architecture.admission: Normal Kernel captures all remaining original Futex/Sleep actors, including frozen tasks, into the same Epoch with actual memory identity and no byte/hardware View.
architecture.demand: Only an actual wake, expiry, signal or control prepares the original mm. Existing execution workers acquire original custody; unrelated executing mms retain their Views. Metadata still allocates.
architecture.custody: Busy original task/mm custody parks on original resource readiness and returns the CPU slot. No new coordinator/resource/service thread or polling bus.
architecture.deadlines: Admitted waiters use changing queue deadlines. Cold Process projections cannot force zero-time host-control polling; actual unowned legacy waits still bound the host-control interval.
architecture.ordering: Existing timer/sleeper expiry publishes scopes before that executor claims lifecycle source work, so the sole executor cannot sleep with its own newly prepared work unclaimed.
architecture.cancellation: Stop before preparation retains original wait identity and accepted wake without constructing byte Views. Frozen wake remains pending until original cgroup thaw.
